::: {#def-causal-model .theorem}
## Causal model

A causal model $\mathcal{C}$ of an NPSEM $\mathcal{M}$ under intervention regime $\Gamma$ is the pair of $\mathcal{M}$ and its interventional NPSEM $\mathcal{M}^{(\Gamma)}$, with the error terms of the two held equal:

$$
\mathcal{C}=\big(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{M}^{(\Gamma)}\big),\qquad U_V^{(\Gamma)}=U_V\quad\text{for all }V\in\mathbf{V}.
$$

Here $U_V$ is the error term of $V$ in $\mathcal{M}$ and $U_V^{(\Gamma)}$ the error term of the corresponding variable in $\mathcal{M}^{(\Gamma)}$.

The variables $\mathbf{V}$ associated with $\mathcal{M}$ are called observational variables; the variables $\mathbf{V}^{(\Gamma)}$ associated with $\mathcal{M}^{(\Gamma)}$ are called counterfactual variables. They are obtained by sequential substitution: in a topological order, each $V^{(\Gamma)}$ is the value of $f_V^{(\Gamma)}$ at the counterfactual values of its parents,

$$
V^{(\Gamma)}=f^{(\Gamma)}_V\big(\mathbf{Pa}(V)^{(\Gamma)},U_V\big).
$$

For an intervened variable $V\in\mathbf{E}$, $V^{(\Gamma)}$ is therefore the value its intervention equation assigns, and it is this value that its children read. Its natural value under $\Gamma$ is $f_V\big(\mathbf{Pa}(V)^{(\Gamma)},U_V\big)$, the value it would have taken had its own equation not been replaced.

Because $\mathcal{M}$ is itself $\mathcal{M}^{(\Gamma)}$ for the empty regime, each observational variable satisfies $V=f_V(\mathbf{Pa}(V),U_V)$. Consistency follows: on the event $\{\mathbf{Pa}(V)=\mathbf{pa}\}$, $V$ equals the one-step-ahead counterfactual $V^{(\mathbf{pa})}=f_V(\mathbf{pa},U_V)$ of C.13.
:::
